parts:
Hi Lavina,

it requires that you have R v2.4.0 or higher (for any analysis always
use at least the latest stable version). I recommend you to use R
v2.4.1. FYI, R and BioC is in the process of being updated to their
next versions during these weeks so behavior might soon change. I am
migrating to R v2.5.0 (alpha) myself, but I am still doing all my
analysis and development on R v2.4.1.

To your error messages; what platform and what version of R are you
running causing those errors? It looks like R v2.4.1, but then it
should work. Could you please forward all of the messages/errors you
get as well as your sessionInfo().

Cheers

Henrik

developer's version of affxparser, i.e. v1.7.3.

messages.subject: Discussion on download-install
parts:
Hello

I have just updated R to R.2.5 and bioconductor (2.0) on my linux
(Ubuntu), so far, so good.
I then installed aroma following the installation guidelines above.
This was fine until:

Loading required package: digest

Error in parse.default(text = src) : 4 arguments passed to 'parse'
which requires 6

Execution halted
ERROR: lazy loading failed for package 'aroma.affymetrix'

** Removing '/usr/local/lib/R/library/aroma.affymetrix'

** Restoring previous '/usr/local/lib/R/library/aroma.affymetrix'
The downloaded packages are in

/tmp/RtmpMWpK4C/downloaded_packages

Warning message:

installation of package 'aroma.affymetrix' had non-zero exit status
in: install.packages(pkg, ..., available = available)

If I then tried to do:
library(aroma.affymetrix)

I received this message:

Loading required package: digest
aroma.affymetrix v0.4.3 (2007-03-15) successfully loaded. See ?
aroma.affymetrix for help.

*** caught segfault ***
address (nil), cause 'memory not mapped'

Traceback:
1: .Call("digest", as.character(object), as.integer(algoint),
as.integer(length), PACKAGE = "digest")
2: digest(0)
3: .assertDigest("error")
4: .setupAromaAffymetrix()
5: f(libname, pkgname)
6: firstlib(which.lib.loc, package)
7: doTryCatch(return(expr), name, parentenv, handler)
8: tryCatchOne(expr, names, parentenv, handlers[[1]])
9: tryCatchList(expr, classes, parentenv, handlers)
10: tryCatch(expr, error = function(e) { call <-
conditionCall(e) if (!is.null(call)) { if
(identical(call[[1]], quote(doTryCatch))) call <-
sys.call(-4) dcall <- deparse(call)[1] prefix <-
paste("Error in", dcall, ": ") LONGCALL <- 30 if
(nchar(dcall) > LONGCALL) prefix <- paste(prefix, "\n\t",
sep = "") } else prefix <- "Error : " msg <- paste(prefix,
conditionMessage(e), "\n", sep =
"") .Internal(seterrmessage(msg[1])) if (!silent &&
identical(getOption("show.error.messages"), TRUE))
{ cat(msg, file =
stderr()) .Internal(printDeferredWarnings()) }
invisible(structure(msg, class = "try-error"))})
11: try(firstlib(which.lib.loc, package))
12: library(aroma.affymetrix)

Possible actions:
1: abort (with core dump, if enabled)
2: normal R exit
3: exit R without saving workspace
4: exit R saving workspace

Any ideas?
cheers

Lavinia.

thanks for this.

Picky moderator ;): not 'aroma' but 'aroma.affymetrix' ; 'aroma' is a
package on two-color arrays.

> This was fine until:
>
> Loading required package: digest
>
> Error in parse.default(text = src) : 4 arguments passed to 'parse'
> which requires 6

I noticed this yesterday too, but in a total different context; to the
best of my understanding this happens when you load an R v2.4.x build
of R.utils in R v2.5.0. It has nothing to do with aroma.affymetrix
per se. You can reproduce the error with:

> library(R.utils)
> parse(text="")

I've committed an update to R.utils that fix the problem. Reinstall
R.utils and try again. The above two lines should now return
"expression()" without an error.

With this fix, the rest of the installation of aroma.affymetrix should
work again.

/Henrik
